item: connect-volume: hardware volume buttons control the Spotify Connect device's volume while PixlAudio is open (foreground only)
currentBehaviour:
Today nothing in the app reacts to the hardware volume buttons during a Connect session. They change the phone's own volume, which does nothing audible because local playback is paused.

Volume path today:
- The only caller is the hero slider `SpotifyConnectVolume` (App/Features/NowPlaying/SpotifyConnectSection.swift:164-207; it sends on release at :189-191, and `.onChange(of: device.volumePercent)` at :203-205 moves the thumb even while the user is dragging). It is shown in the devices sheet hero (App/Features/NowPlaying/DevicesSheet.swift:158-160).
- `SpotifyConnectController.setVolume` (App/Services/Spotify/SpotifyConnectController.swift:679-696) clamps the value, updates `active` and `session` right away, waits 250 ms, then `enqueue`s the request (:500-511).
- `enqueue` is the same serial chain that `send(fromQueueIndex:)` uses (:469-497), and that path also runs `resolveAhead` searches (up to 12 lookups, :306-323). So a volume change can wait seconds behind a window send.
- The request goes through `SpotifyConnectClient.setVolume` (Packages/PixlCore/Sources/PixlNet/Spotify/SpotifyConnectClient.swift:121-123) to `SpotifyConnectAPI.volume`, PUT /v1/me/player/volume?volume_percent&device_id (Packages/PixlCore/Sources/PixlNet/Spotify/SpotifyConnect.swift:141-145). `SpotifyConnectError.volumeNotSupported` already exists (SpotifyConnect.swift:330, mapped from `VOLUME_CONTROL_DISALLOW` at :356).
- There is no `adjustVolume`. Android has one: `SpotifyConnectController.adjustVolume` plus `VOLUME_STEP = 5` and `VOLUME_DEBOUNCE_MS = 250` (android-int-oct3 SpotifyConnectController.kt:853-856, 984-986). Android's own `setVolume` is the same 250 ms trailing debounce through `enqueue` (:829-851). Android gets volume keys natively through Media3 `DeviceInfo.PLAYBACK_TYPE_REMOTE` plus `handleIncrease/DecreaseDeviceVolume` (SpotifyConnectSessionPlayer.kt:102-122, 195-207). So this request is actually Android parity.

Existing problems that would hurt button presses:
- **Polls undo recent changes.** `SpotifyConnectReducer.apply` writes every polled `volume_percent` into the state (Packages/PixlCore/Sources/PixlNet/Spotify/SpotifyConnectSession.swift:154-157), and `publish` copies it into `active` (Controller :423-431). `refreshDevices` does the same from the device list (Controller :145-148). A poll that lands before the PUT takes effect snaps the volume back. The next press then steps from that old value.
- **429 toasts on every press.** The client's 429 gate makes every call fail fast with `.rateLimited` (SpotifyConnectClient.swift:27-34, 53-56), and `report()` shows a toast for each one (Controller :513-528). The poller already sleeps through the gate quietly (:363-364, 382-383).
- **Extra re-renders.** `ActiveDevice` carries `volumePercent` (Controller :27-34). The readers of `active` are `NowPlayingView.outputPill` (App/Features/NowPlaying/NowPlayingView.swift:221, a computed property of NowPlayingView, so the whole player body re-runs), `DevicesSheet.hero` (DevicesSheet.swift:138, 258-259) and `SpotifyConnectSection` (SpotifyConnectSection.swift:23, 77, plus `.animation(..., value: connect.active)` at :41, which opens an animation transaction on every volume change). RootView and the mini player do NOT read `active`.

Audio session while Connect plays:
- `PlaybackStore.attachRemote` only calls `engine.pause()` (App/Stores/PlaybackStore.swift:169-174).
- `DualDeckEngine.pause()` (App/Playback/DualDeckEngine.swift:149-157) keeps the AVAudioSession active. It only gives it back via `releasePreparedActivation()` when nothing is loaded (`activeItem == nil`).
- So the session is active only if something played locally before Connect started. It is not active when:
  - Connect started from a restored, paused queue (`PlaybackServices.restoreQueue`, App/Playback/PlaybackServices.swift:72-76 → `DualDeckEngine.restore` :320-334 sets `playWhenReady = false` and never activates);
  - an interruption happened, which sets `isActive = false` (App/Playback/AudioSessionController.swift:169-176);
  - a paused item load failed, which releases a prepared activation (DualDeckEngine.swift:400-407). This can happen during Connect because `remoteMoved` reloads items (PlaybackStore.swift:191-194).
- `AudioSessionController.deactivate()` is also called directly by `DualDeckEngine.stop()` (:282-290, no app caller found) and on `.abandonFocus` (:611, permanent loss). Those paths should keep dropping the session.
- An active `.playback` session is also what makes the hardware buttons change the media volume (and fire `outputVolume` KVO) instead of the ringer volume.
- Nothing keeps the app alive in the background: no audio plays, so iOS suspends it. The controller already expects this (Controller :775-776).

Related code that already exists:
- `outputVolume` key-value observing: `SystemVolumeObserver` (App/Features/Equalizer/EqualizerView.swift:391-418, also started by DevicesSheet :25, :88-95) and `VolumeZeroPauser` (App/Playback/VolumeZeroPauser.swift:7-35). Both build the handler outside the main actor and hop back with `Task { @MainActor ... }`. `VolumeZeroPauser` only pauses when `engine.active.isPlaying` (PlaybackServices.swift:63-67), which is false during Connect, so it never pauses the remote device.
- Visible `MPVolumeView` sliders: the EQ volume card (EqualizerView.swift:357-389, 420-433) and the hero's phone slider (DevicesSheet.swift:377-390, shown only when no Connect device is active).
- A hidden view already sits in the key window: `PoTokenGenerator` adds its web view with alpha 0.01 (App/Services/YouTube/PoTokenGenerator.swift:91-93; `hostWindow()` at :147-149; docs/api-notes.md:544).
- `UIControl.sendActions(for:)` is already in the ledger (docs/api-notes.md:667). VoiceOver announcements already go through `PixlAccessibility.announce` (App/DesignSystem/AccessibilityAnnouncements.swift:8-11; ledger :695). `UIApplication.applicationState` is already used (App/Services/ML/AutomaticStudioRunner.swift:81) but isn't in the ledger.
- Toast pattern to copy for a new overlay: `LibraryToast` + `LibraryToastOverlay` (App/Features/Library/LibrarySelection.swift:76-126). Its ViewModifier body is the only thing that tracks the model.
- An overlay on RootView (App/Shell/RootView.swift:48 is the Connect toast) covers the tabs and the player sheet. It does NOT cover `.sheet` / `.fullScreenCover` content: the queue is a sheet (App/Shell/RouteDestinations.swift:49) and the lyrics screen is a cover (:68).
- `NowPlayingController` registers MPRemoteCommandCenter commands (App/Playback/NowPlayingController.swift:33-82). There is no volume command to register.
- Wiring point: AppEnvironment (App/AppEnvironment.swift:171-179) connects Connect to Now Playing only for real launches. The UI-test path is :130-149.
- There is no logging facility. Diagnostics is a native `Form` (App/Features/Developer/DiagnosticsView.swift:13-40).
research:
1. **Apple provides no API for this.**
   - Apple staff (Engineer, October 2024): "listening for volume button presses can be accomplished by key-value observing the outputVolume property of AVAudioSession". Otherwise they pointed only to AVCaptureEventInteraction. https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/765821
   - The outputVolume docs (iOS 6+): "Only the user can directly set the system volume. Provide a volume control in your app, using MPVolumeView", and the property can be key-value observed. https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avaudiosession/outputvolume
   - Apple staff (Engineer, June 2024): outputVolume "is read-only, so you cannot change the output volume programmatically". The same thread reports outputVolume values rounded to 0.05 steps, which doesn't match the 16 hardware steps. https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/756484
   - Correction to the previous plan: the 2018 quote "There's a good reason why there isn't any API to detect volume button presses: to prevent apps from doing it" is from QuinceyMorris, a forum veteran **not** marked as Apple staff (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/107241).

2. **What happened to Spotify.**
   - Spotify's iOS app had this feature until September 2024. Spotify said "Apple has discontinued the technology that allows Spotify users to control the volume" and blamed "bugs like volume spikes" (https://techcrunch.com/2024/08/29/spotify-points-finger-at-apple-over-an-unwelcome-change-to-volume-control-technology/). Users are now directed to Spotify's in-app slider. The exact prompt wording in the previous plan is unverified.
   - A developer commenting on https://mjtsai.com/blog/2024/09/05/spotify-connect-can-no-longer-use-iphone-volume-buttons/ says iOS 17.3 broke listening to the private `_UIApplicationVolume*ButtonDownNotification`.
   - John Gruber: "Apple shut those APIs down in iOS 17.6". Marco Arment's guess is that it was the decade-deprecated `MPMusicPlayerController` volume setter, "the only way we've ever been able to programmatically set the iPhone volume" (https://daringfireball.net/linked/2024/09/06/more-on-spotify-connect-and-iphone-volume-buttons).
   - App Review guideline 2.5.9 rejects apps that "alter or disable the functions of standard switches, such as the Volume Up/Down" (https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/). PixlAudio is sideloaded and never reviewed, so this blocks Spotify but not us. It does mean the behaviour is unsupported and can break with any iOS update.

3. **The re-centre trick (setting the volume back after each press).** The usual method is to find the UISlider inside an MPVolumeView and set its value.
   - **Apple DTS (June 2020): "There's no supported way to change the system volume programmatically. Digging into the MPVolumeView view hierarchy wasn't a reliable way to do this, and (as you've seen) it generally doesn't work now."** (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/649183, asked in an AirPlay context). This is the strongest evidence against option A's re-centre.
   - "You are attempting to modify the private view hierarchy of MPVolumeView … you cannot expect this to work" is from TheCD, **not** marked Apple staff (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/105247).
   - Community snippets: a b4x thread (2016, updated 2019 for iOS 11.4+) sets the slider value after a 0.01 s delay, then `sendActionsForControlEvents` (https://www.b4x.com/android/forum/threads/control-general-audio-volume.65118/).
   - I found no report confirming it on iOS 18, 26 or 27. The "more restrictive since iOS 18" quote (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/813242) is about *reading* outputVolume, not about setting it. That developer notes an MPVolumeView "must be added to the UI, otherwise it will always return volume of 0".
   - JPSVolumeButtonHandler (https://github.com/jpsim/JPSVolumeButtonHandler, verified source) re-centres with `[[MPMusicPlayerController applicationMusicPlayer] setVolume:]`. That is the deprecated API (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/mediaplayer/mpmusicplayercontroller/volume) Gruber says was shut down in 17.6.
   - JPS's setup:
     - a `.playback` session with **`MixWithOthers`**, which must be active;
     - an MPVolumeView at frame (MAXFLOAT, MAXFLOAT, 0, 0) in the key window;
     - `Old|New` observation on outputVolume;
     - limits of 0.99999 / 0.00001;
     - re-running setup after a 1 s delay so the system stops showing its own volume pop-up;
     - skipping changes while the app is inactive ("Probably control center").

4. **Hiding the system volume pop-up.** Undocumented. The community technique is an MPVolumeView in the window, not hidden, with alpha > 0, even off-screen: b4x uses frame (-2000, -2000, 0, 0), alpha 0.1 and `userInteractionEnabled = NO`; JPS uses a MAXFLOAT frame. The previous plan's quoted wording had no real source.
   - iOS 26 and 27 behaviour with the new volume pop-up is unverified.
   - Known iOS 18 bugs:
     - outputVolume is stale after the session is deactivated and reactivated. DTS (September 2025): "there is no known workaround" (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/799104).
     - Changes made in the background aren't seen (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/813242).
     - The first read can return 0 (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/764731; Apple asked for a bug report, no workaround).
     - Developers' workaround is a real MPVolumeView in the UI.
   - The Simulator can't change the volume at all: "You can't change the volume or choose a route with this class while testing in the Simulator" (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/mediaplayer/mpvolumeview). So this can only be tested on the phone.

5. **Rejected alternatives:**
   - AVCaptureEventInteraction (iOS 17.2) and SwiftUI `onCameraCaptureEvent`: "You can only use this API for capture use cases. The system sends capture events only to apps that actively use the camera." (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avkit/avcaptureeventinteraction). WWDC25 session 253 adds "those that do not have an active AVCaptureSession running, won't receive any events" (https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2025/253/). Not usable for a music app.
   - MPRemoteCommandCenter has no volume command (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/mediaplayer/mpremotecommandcenter).
   - MPNowPlayingSession (iOS 16) only handles Now Playing info and remote commands for AVPlayers (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/mediaplayer/mpnowplayingsession).
   - AVRouting:
     - AVCustomRoutingController has no volume API, and custom routes need a DeviceDiscoveryExtension app extension, which free-ID signing forbids (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avrouting , https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicediscoveryextension).
     - AVRoutingPlaybackArbiter (AVRouting, iOS 26) only "manages playback routing preferences" (priorities on non-mixable routes and external playback). Verified: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avrouting/avroutingplaybackarbiter
   - Making the session mixable during Connect, as JPS does: it would avoid interrupting other audio. But PixlAudio's category uses the `.longFormAudio` route-sharing policy (AudioSessionController.swift:67-73), and the Connect lock-screen controls rely on PixlAudio staying the Now Playing app. Changing the category mid-session is untested risk, so the plan keeps the non-mixable session plus guards.
   - Playing silent audio to keep observing in the background or on the lock screen costs battery and takes over other apps' audio. Not recommended.
   - iOS 27 adds separate ringtone, alarm and notification volume sliders (https://appleosophy.com/2026/06/08/ios-27-features-separate-volume-controls-for-ringtone-alarms-and-notifications/). There is still no public API for third-party remote-volume buttons.

6. **Rate limits.** Spotify's limit is a rolling 30-second window shared with the existing 1-second poll (docs/api-notes.md:740). The existing 429 gate is clamped to 1-60 s (SpotifyConnect.swift:331).

options.name: A. Observe outputVolume, hide the system pop-up, re-centre with a hidden MPVolumeView slider, own glass pop-up, foreground only (recommended to try, with automatic fallback to B)
options.description:
While a Connect session runs on a device that supports volume and the app is active:
- Hold the AVAudioSession active.
- Add a 1×1 pt, alpha 0.01 MPVolumeView off-screen in the key window. This suppresses the system volume pop-up.
- Observe outputVolume with `[.old, .new]`. Turn each change of about one step (|Δ| in 0.03-0.13; iPhone steps are 1/16, reported rounded to about 0.05) into ±1 press, which moves the device by ±5% (Android VOLUME_STEP).
- Set the phone volume back to a centre value through the hidden view's UISlider, and ignore the change that reset causes. The centre is the user's own volume snapped to the 1/16 grid and clamped to 2/16-14/16.
- If no echo of the reset arrives within 500 ms and outputVolume isn't within 0.035 of the centre, switch automatically to option B for the rest of the session.
- Show PixlAudio's own glass volume pop-up.
- On resign-active (Control Center), pause press handling and put the phone volume back. On background, session end or loss of volume support, remove the hidden view and release the session.
options.pros: Fixed 5% steps at any phone volume. No drift to 0 or 1. Matches Android. The hero slider and the pop-up follow live. Degrades on its own instead of breaking.
options.cons: Undocumented. Apple DTS said in 2020 that setting MPVolumeView's slider 'generally doesn't work now', and the MPMusicPlayerController route was shut down in 17.6. Hiding the pop-up is also undocumented and unverified for the iOS 26/27 pop-up. Must be checked on Hoa's phone; the Simulator can't test it. Realistically B is the floor.

options.name: B. Observe outputVolume only, relative steps, no re-centre (public APIs only)
options.description: Same observation and hidden MPVolumeView. Each change of about one step becomes ±5% on the device, but the phone volume is never set back.
options.pros: Uses only public APIs plus an MPVolumeView placed in the view hierarchy. This is the approach DTS described in 2024. Nothing undocumented is touched except the pop-up hiding.
options.cons: Once the phone volume reaches 1.0 (or 0), further presses in that direction produce no change and no KVO event, so the device stops moving and there is no feedback. Mitigate with a one-time toast: 'Use the slider in Devices to go further'. The phone's own volume is left changed. Best kept as A's automatic fallback.

options.name: C. Absolute or proportional mapping of phone volume onto device volume
options.description: Device % = phone volume × 100, or scale the remaining range up or down per press.
options.cons: The first press can jump the speaker by up to 60 points. Near the ends, proportional mapping turns one press into a jump to 100%. That is the 'volume spikes' risk. Rejected.

options.name: D. Spotify-style prompt
options.description: Observe outputVolume. On a press, show a glass toast 'Change <device> volume?' that opens the devices sheet hero slider.
options.pros: Fully public and stable. Close to what Spotify does today.
options.cons: Not what Hoa asked for. The phone volume still changes and the system pop-up still shows.

options.name: E. Deprecated MPMusicPlayerController.applicationMusicPlayer.volume setter for the re-centre
options.description: The JPSVolumeButtonHandler technique (verified in its source).
options.cons: Deprecated since iOS 7. Per Gruber and Arment (Daring Fireball, 2024) this is very likely exactly what Apple shut down in iOS 17.6. It also touches the system music player. Rejected.

options.name: F. AVCaptureEventInteraction / onCameraCaptureEvent
options.cons: Needs a running AVCaptureSession (the camera). Events go only to apps that are actively capturing. Not viable.

options.name: G. Background or lock-screen support with silent audio
options.description: Keep a silent local stream playing so observation continues after the app leaves the foreground.
options.cons: Battery drain, takes over other apps' audio and the Now Playing state, against the platform's intent. Hoa asked for 'while in the app' only.

recommendedPlan.change:
- Add `public var volumeHoldUntilMs: Int64` to `SpotifyConnectSessionState`, with a defaulted `volumeHoldUntilMs: Int64 = 0` init parameter at the end (lines 33-36), so existing call sites and tests keep compiling. Hashable stays synthesized.
- Add `public static let volumeHoldMs: Int64 = 3000` and `public static func setVolume(_ percent: Int, _ state: inout SpotifyConnectSessionState, nowMs: Int64)` to `SpotifyConnectReducer` (next to `setPlaying` at :200). It clamps to 0...100, sets `volumePercent`, and sets `volumeHoldUntilMs = nowMs + volumeHoldMs`.
- In `apply` (lines 154-157), skip the polled `volume_percent` while `nowMs < state.volumeHoldUntilMs`, so stale polls no longer snap the volume back.

recommendedPlan.file: Packages/PixlCore/Sources/PixlNet/Spotify/SpotifyConnectVolume.swift (new, pure Swift, Sendable, Windows-safe, Foundation only)

recommendedPlan.change:
- Add `case nowPlayingSpotifyVolumeHUD = "nowPlaying.spotifyVolumeHUD"`.
  - Add it to `cover` (→ `.nowPlaying`, like `.nowPlayingSpotifyConnect` at :240) and to `startsSpotifyConnectSession` (:231-235).
  - NOT to `opensOverPlayer`: that list is for sheets over the expanded player (:214-219). `readyIdentifier` then resolves to `screen.nowPlaying`.
- In `startDemoSessionIfNeeded` (:798-801), when the screen is the HUD screen, call `volumeHUD.show(percent: 45, deviceName: "Kitchen Echo Show", pinned: true)`, so the screenshot doesn't race the 1.5 s hide.
- Add `testVolumeHUDLight` and `testVolumeHUDDark`, which wait for `spotifyConnect.volumeHUD`.
- The real button handling can't run in the Simulator (MPVolumeView docs).

recommendedPlan.file: docs/api-notes.md, docs/parity.md (row 33, line 33), docs/test-parity.md, docs/design.md (Spotify Connect section, line 713), docs/handoff/<today's date>-connect-volume.md

risks: The re-centre and pop-up hiding are undocumented. Apple DTS said in 2020 that setting MPVolumeView's slider 'generally doesn't work now' (forum thread 649183), and the MPMusicPlayerController route was shut down in iOS 17.6. iOS 26/27 behaviour is unverified, and the Simulator can't change the volume. Mitigation: the echo check falls back to option B automatically, Diagnostics shows the mode, and it must be tested on Hoa's iOS 27 phone before the parity row moves. Expect B (works until the phone volume hits an end) as the realistic floor.

Activating a non-mixable `.playback` session to receive button presses interrupts other audio playing on this phone. If the Connect target is this phone's own Spotify app, it would stop that audio. Guards: `secondaryAudioShouldBeSilencedHint`, excluding Smartphone/Tablet device types, and not reactivating on Control Center pulls. A Connect target on another phone would also lose button control; that's acceptable.

iOS 18+ outputVolume bugs: stale after the session is reactivated (DTS: no known workaround), an initial read of 0, and values rounded to about 0.05. Read the starting value from the hidden slider after layout, keep the session active through resign-active, use a 0.035 echo tolerance, and let a mismatched first change re-anchor. One press may be lost after each return from the background.

False or lost presses: Control Center (the app is inactive, so changes are ignored), route changes such as headphones (re-anchor), and in-app MPVolumeView drags (delta filter). A down press landing exactly while a reset echo is pending looks like the echo and is dropped. If iOS 27 changes the per-press step away from 1/16, the 0.03-0.13 window must be retuned; Diagnostics shows the last delta.

Some speakers round `volume_percent` (Echo, TVs). After the 3 s hold, a single 5% press may read back as unchanged and seem to stall. The hold keeps quick bursts on the local target. Check this on a real Echo, and if needed bump the step for that device.

Rate limits: Spotify's rolling 30 s window is shared with the 1 s poll, and dev-mode quotas are per developer account. The lane caps volume PUTs at about 3/s during a held button and coalesces to the latest value. A 429 waits Retry-After quietly. Never send one PUT per change without throttling.
Volume spikes, as reported with Spotify's old hack: never map absolute phone volume, move only ±1-2 steps per change, clamp to 0...100.

If the restore in `stop()` or on resign-active fails, the phone's own volume stays at the centre value. The centre equals the user's volume snapped to 1/16 unless it was below 0.125 or above 0.875, which limits the impact.
Call order in `finish`: releasing the hold before `playback.resumeLocally` would deactivate (telling other apps to resume) and then immediately reactivate. The plan releases after it.

This adds new UI (the volume pop-up) beyond strict Android parity. Hoa asked for the behaviour, so his request overrides. The pop-up must follow the Liquid Glass rules: one glass layer, a fill bar inside, Reduce Motion and Reduce Transparency respected. It needs the overlay in three places (RootView, SheetDestination, CoverDestination), or it won't show on the lyrics screen or the queue.

Overlap with Hoa's other item, 'remove the Now Playing word and cloud icon to show the connected device's name'. It edits the same NowPlayingView top bar (outputPill reads `spotifyConnect.active` at :221). Splitting `volumePercent` out of `ActiveDevice` touches the same code, so coordinate the two edits. Also coordinate with the 'more Liquid Glass on the queue/lyrics' items, which edit the same SheetDestination/CoverDestination views.

Main-thread cost: the observation hops to the main actor, and only the pop-up modifier, the hero slider and the EQ card re-render. Adding and removing the hidden view happens at most once per foreground cycle.
Nothing compiles locally. Check the new APIs (`secondaryAudioShouldBeSilencedHint`, `observe` with `.old`, `UISlider.setValue(_:animated:)`) on CI, and record them in docs/api-notes.md.
ownerDecisions: Is the undocumented 'reset the phone volume after each press' trick OK? It touches MPVolumeView's internal slider, which Apple says generally doesn't work and Spotify had to drop, but a sideloaded build isn't reviewed. (a) Try it, with an automatic fallback to (b) (recommended). (b) Public APIs only: presses work until the phone's own volume reaches max or min, then a toast points to the slider. (c) Spotify-style: a press shows a glass 'Change <device> volume?' toast that opens the slider.

Foreground only, as you described? It stops on the lock screen and in the background, and pauses while Control Center is open. Background support needs a silent audio loop, which isn't recommended. Suggest: foreground only.
Step per press: 5% (same as Android, recommended) or 6% (about 1/16, closer to the iPhone's own steps)?

PixlAudio's own glass volume pop-up instead of the system one: top centre (recommended) or top left near the buttons? It will show over the full player, the lyrics screen and sheets such as the queue. Should it stay hidden while the devices sheet is open, where the slider already moves?

Always on (recommended, in line with your 'hardcode it' preference elsewhere), or a Settings › Playback toggle 'Volume buttons control Spotify Connect devices'? A toggle also means touching SettingsStore and backup.
Leave out Connect devices of type Smartphone or Tablet (for example, this iPhone's own Spotify app), so PixlAudio never interrupts its audio? Suggest: yes.
While a Connect device plays, should the Equalizer's volume card switch to the device's volume (suggested), or keep showing the phone's volume?
newAppleAPIs: AVAudioSession.secondaryAudioShouldBeSilencedHint, iOS 8.0 (verified: 'whether another app, with a nonmixable audio session, is playing audio'). https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avaudiosession/secondaryaudioshouldbesilencedhint (alternatively AVAudioSession.isOtherAudioPlaying, iOS 6.0, https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avaudiosession/isotheraudioplaying). Used to skip activation when other audio is playing.

NSObject.observe(_:options:changeHandler:) with NSKeyValueObservingOptions [.old, .new] on AVAudioSession.outputVolume, iOS 6 / Swift 4. https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio/avaudiosession/outputvolume. The ledger only lists `.new` (api-notes line 402).

MPVolumeView placed hidden in the key window (alpha 0.01, off-screen) to suppress the system volume pop-up, iOS 2.0. https://developer.apple.com/documentation/mediaplayer/mpvolumeview. MPVolumeView itself is ledgered (lines 401, 436). The suppression is undocumented behaviour (b4x 2016, JPSVolumeButtonHandler); the window-hosting pattern is already in the ledger at line 544.

UISlider.setValue(_:animated:), iOS 2.0, on MPVolumeView's internal slider. https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uislider/setvalue(_:animated:). Reaching into the private hierarchy is undocumented (DTS 2020: 'generally doesn't work now', https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/649183); it is guarded by the fallback. UIControl.sendActions(for:) is already ledgered (line 667); record the new use only.

UIApplication.applicationState, iOS 4.0. https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uiapplication/applicationstate. Already used in AutomaticStudioRunner.swift:81 but missing from the ledger. willResignActive/didBecomeActive are already ledgered (line 699).
screenshotTests: SettingsScreenshotTests/testEqualizerGraphModeLight (regression check of the EQ volume card)
